commit.message:
desktop: fix pin desync, fullscreen/maximize pin corruption, drag dead-ends

Plain pin/unpin "didn't stay toggled" and the window could lose its only
drag handle. Root cause: pin state lived in three stores that could drift
and never re-sync — window_on_top is echoed only on change, unlike the
heartbeat-backed pause/volume controls the pattern was copied from.

Frontend (App.tsx):
- One optimistic value (`pinned`/`onTopRef`) now drives BOTH the button
  highlight and the next-command direction, so the button responds
  instantly instead of waiting a status round-trip (the lag is what made
  it feel like the toggle "didn't take").
- Roll the optimistic value back to host truth when a /stay-on-top POST
  fails (and surface a toast), so a lost command can't strand the toggle
  direction against the idempotent host.
- Gate the pin-mode surface drag on the host-confirmed window_on_top
  (hostOnTopRef) — the same truth the host's nc_hit uses — so the window
  always has exactly one drag handle, never zero.
- Auto-hide gate uses optimistic displayPaused (no flash on Space).

Host (compositor.rs):
- Fullscreen exit re-applies HWND_TOPMOST from the live is_on_top, so a
  pin done while fullscreen no longer leaves the titlebar gone forever.
- Pin entry clears WS_MAXIMIZE (SW_RESTORE) before the aspect snap, so
  maximized->pin keeps working resize borders.
- WM_GETMINMAXINFO floors the window above its own chrome width.
- After a pin-mode modal move loop, nudge the overlay so the control bar
  (the only mouse unpin affordance in pin mode) reveals.
- Persist the pre-pin windowed rect, not the aspect-snapped pin rect.

Docs: add the "Pin toggle: one click, one command" contract section that
desktop-shell.md already linked to; refresh ADR-0001's outstanding note.

desktop: flush SSE status frames so the last change before idle is delivered

The titlebar never returned after unpinning while the video was paused. The
root cause was in the status stream, not the pin logic: tiny_http buffers the
response in a 1024-byte BufWriter and never flushes a streaming body, so a
sub-1 KiB status frame sits unsent until enough following bytes overflow the
buffer. With a paused video no further frames follow, so the unpin's
window_on_top=false never reached the overlay — it stayed "pinned" (titlebar
hidden, video-surface drag armed) even though the host had already unpinned.
This is pre-existing and is why the earlier frontend work couldn't cure it.

Fix: when the status stream would idle after delivering a frame, emit a >1 KiB
SSE comment (clients ignore ':'-prefixed lines) so the BufWriter overflows and
pushes that frame to the socket at once. Verified with a live SSE capture: the
unpin's false now arrives ~150ms after the POST instead of never; unit test
locks the idle-flush behavior.
